column3: It joins the no-deity formula to Allah as Creator of every thing and its guardian, closely grounding exclusive divinity in universal authority.
Creation of every thing by measure supports the comprehensive order behind the focus, though it does not state divine knowledge or exclusive deityhood.
It affirms one deity across heaven and earth and names Him the Wise, Knowing, directly reinforcing the focus's universal divine identity.
It closely repeats Allah as the sole deity and Creator of every thing, making the focus's exclusive claim concrete through creation.
Musa's questioning of the Samiri is immediate narrative context for the correction of the calf's false divinity.
Allah's knowledge is affirmed, but the verse does not develop the focus's exclusive deityhood or comprehensive scope.
The same no-deity formula is explicitly paired with knowledge of the unseen and seen, a close expansion of encompassing knowledge.
Exclusive worship of Allah and His witness over every thing support the focus's authority claim, though in a different prophetic setting.
It rejects partners and exactly states that the Lord encompasses every thing in knowledge, making it one of the closest parallels.
It forbids another deity beside Allah and places all things under His final judgment and return.
The Samiri's account belongs to the same immediate episode and explains the act that necessitates the final theological correction.
The expansion of the heaven does not clarify the focus's claim about knowledge encompassing every thing.

The revealed message that the deity is one reiterates the focus's central exclusivity claim.

Revelation being sent with Allah's knowledge gives general support to divine knowledge but not its universal scope.

The recording of every thing offers a useful but indirect image of total enumeration.
Ignorance of revealed limits among desert Arabs does not explain the focus's universal knowledge or exclusive deityhood.
Worship of the Lord to whom every thing belongs supports universal lordship, though it lacks the explicit knowledge formula.
Household privacy rules and Allah's knowledge do not add a focused relation to the verse.
The sleepers defer their duration to their Lord's knowledge, a narrow instance of human knowledge being limited.

The household eating permissions do not clarify exclusive divinity or encompassing knowledge.

The granted knowledge of Dawud and Sulayman is a creaturely gift, not an account of Allah's comprehensive knowledge.
The deniers' rejection of warning does not develop the focus's deity or knowledge claim.
Human knowledge is limited while the Lord knows guidance and error, giving a useful contrast to divine comprehensive knowledge.
Allah's knowledge of people from their origin and of the pious provides a concrete, though partial, knowledge parallel.
The punishment of disbelievers does not clarify the focus's claim.
The promise that people will know later does not add to Allah's encompassing knowledge.
Religious factions and their final return to Allah do not directly explain the focus's correction of false deityhood.
Fear of the unseen concerns human response, not Allah's comprehensive knowledge.
The eventual knowledge of those distracted by worldly enjoyment has no focused relation to the verse.

The questioning of entrants to Hell does not clarify the focus.
Each soul knowing what it brought is a judgment context with only an indirect total-knowledge parallel.
It states that Allah knows what lies before and behind people while they cannot encompass Him in knowledge, directly clarifying the asymmetry in 20:98.
Allah as Knowing and Wise in a legal ruling does not develop the focus's universal scope.
The warning that people will know later does not provide a useful neighbor relation.
The one-deity and no-deity formula directly reinforces the focus's exclusivity, though it adds mercy rather than encompassing knowledge.
Divorce and nursing provisions do not clarify the focus's theological claim.

Allah's being the ever-living, self-sustaining sole deity reinforces the exclusive identity asserted in the focus.
Divine sovereignty and power over every thing support the universal authority implied by encompassing knowledge.
Knowledge of the unseen of heaven and earth and of deeds gives a concrete scope parallel to the focus.
Allah's testimony to His sole deityhood, joined by angels and people of knowledge, reinforces exclusivity with an evidentiary frame.
Creation of life and death for testing does not clarify the focus's exclusive deityhood or comprehensive knowledge.

The command to fear Allah in Lot's scene does not clarify the focus.

Allah as the wisest judge gives only a broad authority parallel.
Allah alone as Lord of the mighty throne directly reinforces sole deityhood and supreme rule.
The disclosure of a secret by the Knowing, Aware supports the focus's claim that knowledge is not limited by concealment.

Divorce regulations and divine limits do not clarify the focus.

It repeats that no deity exists except Allah and gives sovereign names that expand His exclusive authority.
Mary's faithfulness does not clarify the focus's exclusive deityhood or encompassing knowledge.
Allah's hearing and knowledge in a temptation response give only a narrow knowledge parallel.
It explicitly forbids taking two deities and declares that He is one deity, directly reinforcing the focus's exclusivity.
The command to protect families from the Fire does not clarify the focus.
The insistence on retaining named false gods provides a clear counterexample to the exclusive deityhood asserted in the focus.
Exclusive worship of Allah makes the practical allegiance required by the focus's sole-deity declaration explicit.
Allah's hearing and knowledge are affirmed, but without the universal scope central to the focus.

Allah's knowledge of the Prophet's distress gives a personal instance, not comprehensive knowledge.
The command to fear Allah and obey a messenger does not clarify the focus.
Allah's hearing and knowledge support a general divine knowledge frame but not its comprehensive scope.
The call to recognize Allah's majesty does not develop exclusive deityhood or encompassing knowledge.
The Lord knows both what hearts conceal and what people disclose, concretely supporting comprehensive knowledge.
Family nursing rules and Allah's sight of deeds do not give a focused neighbor relation.
The challenge to seeking false gods apart from Allah directly contrasts with the focus's categorical rejection of rival deities.
It records Israel taking the calf during Musa's appointed absence, supplying the earlier occurrence of the false worship corrected in the focus.
Musa commands repentance to the Creator after the calf worship, directly setting the false object against its true Creator.
It explicitly recalls that Israel took the calf after clear signs, giving a close prior instance of the error resolved by 20:98.
Allah's possession of heaven and earth and encompassing of every thing supply a direct universal-authority parallel.
The keys of the unseen and exhaustive knowledge of every leaf and grain concretely unfold what it means for nothing to escape divine knowledge.
Musa rejects seeking any god other than Allah, directly anticipating the exclusive-deity correction after the calf episode.
The calf neither spoke nor guided, exposing the incapacity of the false object opposed to the all-knowing true God.
The Israelites recognize their error after taking the calf and appeal for mercy, giving the immediate human response to the false worship.
Musa returns angry and seizes Harun after the calf worship, extending the episode's corrective confrontation.
It states the consequence for those who took the calf, making the rejection of its alleged divinity explicit in the parallel narrative.
The promise of forgiveness after evil and repentance supplies the restorative aftermath of the calf transgression.
No action, recitation, or smallest thing is absent from the Lord's witnessing record, strongly illustrating all-encompassing knowledge.
Allah identifies the people as tested after Musa's departure and names the Samiri as the agent of their misguidance, directly opening the focus episode.
Musa's angry return confronts the people's breach of the divine promise, immediately preceding the exposure of the calf's false claim.
The people explain how the ornaments were cast and the Samiri threw them, supplying the material origin of the false object.
The Samiri presents the lowing calf as the people's god and Musa's god, the precise false claim that 20:98 refutes.
The calf cannot answer, harm, or benefit them, directly contrasting its incapacity with the true God's comprehensive knowledge.
Harun warns that the calf is a test and calls the people to follow him and obey the Most Merciful, forming the immediate alternative to its worship.
The people's insistence on continuing the calf's worship until Musa returns makes the rival allegiance corrected in 20:98 explicit.
Musa's rebuke of Harun continues the immediate reckoning over the calf worship, though it adds less to the theological claim itself.
The question of why Harun did not follow Musa develops the episode's internal responsibility rather than the focus's knowledge claim.
Harun explains that he feared dividing Israel, completing the immediate narrative exchange before Musa turns to the Samiri.
Not even an atom in heaven or earth escapes Allah's knowledge, a close concrete formulation of knowledge encompassing every thing.
It explicitly declares that Allah encompasses every thing, giving a near verbal parallel to the focus's closing totality.
Allah knows all that is in heaven and earth and every private counsel, directly exemplifying universal, inescapable knowledge.
